sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.

sources_quoted.note: The cached atom decomposition independently types Unmake as a magic-damage-family behavior, not an all-damage amplifier.

sources_quoted.text: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.note: Contrast case: Mandate amplifies ALL damage types (7%), Abyssal amplifies MAGIC only (12%). The scenario name pairs both, so the corpus is built to exercise exactly this discrimination.

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|magic damage}} to an enemy champion with a [[champion ability]] applies a stack of ''Vile Decay'' ... Each stack inflicts {{as|{{fd|7.5}}% magic resistance reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|mr}} at 4 stacks.
sources_quoted.note: The "curse" token in the scenario id resolves to this third support item; it is an MR-reduction effect, NOT a damage multiplier, so it can never author a support_damage_multiplier leaf. It therefore cannot explain the removed 1.12.

sources_quoted.text: No section, formula, or audit-table row covers ally/support damage-amplification auras (grep: 'abyssal', 'unmake', 'mandate', 'support_damage_multiplier', 'aura', '700' — zero hits). The document therefore neither supports nor contradicts either value; the wiki cache is the only governing source.

No scenario with id 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' (and no Abyssal/Mandate scenario at all); the golden corpus definition lives outside the permitted evidence tree, so the damage TYPE of events[13] could not be read directly.

rule_derived_from_wiki_text: Unmake is an aura with two independent gates, both stated in the one sentence:
gate 1 (target/position): the target must be an ENEMY CHAMPION within 700 units (center-to-edge) of the Abyssal Mask holder — i.e. cursed.
gate 2 (damage type): the amplified quantity is '12% increased MAGIC damage'. 'from all sources' widens the SOURCE of the damage (any ally, any item, any DoT), it does not widen the TYPE.
Multiplier form: m_abyssal = 1 + 0.12 = 1.12, applied to magic-damage instances only.
Physical and true damage instances receive m = 1.00 from Unmake, i.e. no multiplier leaf at all.
cross_check_on_the_old_leaf_shape: The old leaf carried a bare 1.12 with a single source string and no Imperial Mandate term.
If Mandate's Vulnerable window had been live at events[13], the amps would compose multiplicatively: 1.12 × 1.07 = 1.1984.
So events[13] sits outside the 4 s Vulnerable window, and Unmake's aura — which is unconditional in time — was the only amp the old baseline claimed.

Within a single fight against a single cursed target, the ONLY per-event discriminator available in the wiki text is gate 2, the damage type. An unconditional positional aura cannot legitimately be on for events 0..12 and off for event 13; a magic-only gate can, and that is precisely what fires when event 13 is a physical or true damage instance (or a non-damage ledger row such as a heal/shield event, where a damage multiplier is meaningless).
independent_computation.conclusion: Correct value of combat/events[13]/support_damage_multiplier = 1.12 IF AND ONLY IF events[13] is a magic-damage instance landed on a cursed enemy champion; otherwise the leaf must be absent (m = 1.00). The evidence tree permitted to this oracle does not expose the damage type of events[13] directly, so the determination is made structurally: a single-event removal of an otherwise time-unconditional aura is explicable only by the magic-only gate (or by the row not being a damage row), and is not explicable by any reading of the cached Unmake text that would keep 1.12 there.

residual_uncertainty: events[13]'s damage type could not be read (scenario definition and golden baseline live under scripts/, outside the permitted evidence tree). The verdict rests on the structural argument above: every reading of the cached wiki text that removes Unmake from exactly one event of one fight is a damage-type (or non-damage-row) gate, and each such reading makes the removal correct; the only way the old 1.12 survives is if events[13] is magic damage, which would require the new code to drop a time-unconditional aura for a single event — a shape no cached source supports.
